title: Professional Frontend State Architecture
outcome: Choose the correct owner for URL state, server state, local UI state, forms, and global client state instead of duplicating everything.
artifact: A state ownership map for TaskFlow plus refactored examples removing redundant synchronized state.
labSteps: Inventory every state variable on one TaskFlow screen and classify it: server, URL, form, local UI, or cross-cutting client.
Move filter/search/page state that should survive/share navigation into URL search params.
Remove local copies of TanStack Query data and derive filtered/presentational values during render.
Keep ephemeral dialog/menu state at the smallest component that owns it.
Evaluate whether any global store is actually needed; write the requirement before adding one.
Create a diagram showing source of truth and allowed data flow for the screen.
failureModes: useEffect syncing query data into local state
Global store used for all state categories
URL and React state disagreeing about filters
Storing derived values that can be computed
mastery: Can classify state before choosing library
Can use URL for shareable navigation state
Can justify any global client store
principles: Put shareable navigation state in the URL, server state in TanStack Query, and local interaction state near the component that owns it.
Avoid duplicating the same piece of state across URL, React state, and query cache.
Derive values when possible instead of synchronizing multiple mutable copies.
Choose state ownership by lifecycle and source of truth, not by whichever library is fashionable.
